messages:
anya: Heads-up — saw a regression after yesterday's kernel-selector change. Several 32k-context requests hit OOM on prod-gpu-03. Not all requests, seems correlated with long-prefill + concurrent batches.

miguel: Can you paste the logs and the selector config you rolled?

anya: Logs snippet from prod-gpu-03 around the failure: ```
[2025-02-03T14:12:11Z] INFO kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=attn_fused_v2 workspace_req=624MB
[2025-02-03T14:12:11Z] WARN allocator: failed_allocating_workspace size=655360000 err=OOM
[2025-02-03T14:12:11Z] ERROR runtime: request_id=abc123 fatal=OOM during decode
```
Looks like the fused kernel bumped workspace requirements, the allocator didn't reclaim fragmented buffers fast enough.

ops-bot: deploy-hook: kernel-selector v2.1 rolled to prod (commit b4c2a7f) at 2025-02-03T13:50:00Z — impacting 2 regions.

kevin: Two immediate ideas: 1) cap workspace per-stream and fall back to a lower-memory kernel; 2) enable aggressive buffer reuse (keep a small freelist for temp tensors). I sketched a patch in my branch `allocator/freelist-timeout`.

sasha: Also related: KV cache prefill vs decode strategy. If we prefill large prefix for many concurrent requests, combined KV + workspace blows past GPU mem. We should enforce per-request KV caps and consider evict-on-prefill with background decode fallback. Prefill-heavy workloads fragment memory more.

dave: Profiling dump (shortened): ```
model: redwood-3b-q4
concurrent_streams: 12
avg_seq_len: 25000
peak_allocated: 30.7GB
fragmentation_metric: 0.32 (measured as free_blocks / total_blocks)
kv_cache_alloc: 6.4GB (per-host aggregated)
workspaces_reserved: 9.2GB (due to fused kernels)
```
Repro: `bazel run //runtime/integration:test_kv_prefill -- --concurrency=12 --seq=25000`

miguel: Quick mitigations we can flip without a release: set REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_MAX=512MB, enable REDWOOD_ALLOC_REUSE=1, and set per-request KV hard cap (env) to 1M tokens. Try: `export REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_MAX=536870912; export REDWOOD_ALLOC_REUSE=1; ./start-runtime --kv-hard-cap=1000000`

anya: Ran the env change on a staging node. OOMs stopped for the 32k repro, but token/s throughput dropped ~11% for high-prefill flows. Numbers: baseline 720 tok/s -> 640 tok/s. Latency tail improved though (p99 down 18%).

sasha: Tradeoff expected. For long-term: (a) adaptive workspace sizing per-model + per-seq-distribution, (b) smarter eviction: hybrid slab LRU for KV (prefill slabs evict first), (c) kernel selection policy that considers both workspace and fragmentation (not just peak mem/latency). Also track decode vs prefill hit rates in console.

kevin: I'll open an RFC with a proposal: allocator freelist + timed purge, per-request kv caps + evict priority, and a kernel-fallback policy when workspace can't be satisfied. Add benchmarks for 4k/32k flows.

anya: @kevin please tag eng-sre and eng-ml. I'll attach the repro traces and the perf numbers. Also adding a note: if we fallback kernels too eagerly we must preserve output parity tests.

miguel: Agreed. Short-term: ops flips in canary with env knobs. Medium-term: implement freelist timeout + eviction policy. Long-term: runtime autoscaler that knows sequence-length distributions.

kevin: PR/issue tracker link will be in the RFC, plus a perf dashboard. Pinging the perf-alerts channel when it's live. :thumbsup:

sasha: Also leaving a pointer to the internal doc for prior KV experiments: <https://redwood.internal/docs/kv-eviction> (notes on prefill vs decode).

anya: Cool — thanks all. Will update after the canary run finishes.
